issues.t: Diesel EGR cooler cracks and leaks coolant into the engine
issues.sym: Coolant level dropping with no outside leak, an overheating warning, or white smoke from the exhaust on start-up.
issues.why: The EGR cooler on the 3.2L diesel cools exhaust gas with engine coolant. Repeated heating and cooling can crack it inside, so coolant is pulled into the cylinders. Ford launched a replacement program (21M03) for affected vans.
issues.next: Stop driving if it overheats. Coolant in the cylinders can lock up and destroy the engine. Ask a Ford dealer whether program 21M03 covers your VIN.

issues.t: Diesel fuel injection pump can fail and stall the van (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls while driving or will not start, without much warning.
issues.why: On about 2,000 vans built at Kansas City from July 2015 to April 2016, the diesel fuel injection pump could fail and send metal debris through the fuel system. NHTSA recall 16V-618.
issues.next: If it stalls, steer to a safe spot with the hazard lights on. Check your VIN; the dealer replaces the pump, and the injectors too if debris is found, for free.

issues.t: Diesel particulate filter clogs and 'Drive to Clean' warnings
issues.sym: A 'Drive to Clean' message, check engine light (codes like P2459 or P2463), reduced power or limp mode.
issues.why: The diesel particulate filter traps soot and has to burn it off at high exhaust temperatures. Short trips, idling and stop-and-go delivery work keep it from getting hot enough. A failed fuel vaporizer glow plug that helps with regeneration and a cracked filter are also known causes.
issues.next: When the message appears, drive at steady highway speed for 20 minutes or so if you can. If it keeps coming back, have the soot level and the vaporizer glow plug checked before the filter gets damaged.

issues.t: NOx sensor or SCR catalyst failure on the diesel
issues.sym: Check engine light, a warning about the emissions system or DEF, and possibly a countdown to reduced speed.
issues.why: The 3.2L diesel's NOx sensors and SCR catalyst (the parts that clean exhaust using DEF fluid) fail often enough that Ford extended their warranty coverage (programs 21N02, 21N05 and 21N06).
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask a Ford dealer whether the extended warranty covers your van before paying for parts.

issues.t: Water gets into the air intake and causes misfires
issues.sym: Hard starts, misfires, low power or limp mode after rain or a car wash, and a wet air filter.
issues.why: Water can get past the cowl seal below the windshield and into the air intake. Ford's fix (TSB 19-2091, vans built before late July 2018) adds water deflectors, seals and a revised air cleaner cover.
issues.next: Check the air filter for water after heavy rain. Have a Ford dealer install the bulletin parts before water does real engine damage.

issues.t: Overheating from coolant deposits clogging the radiator
issues.sym: Engine or transmission temperature warnings, especially when loaded, towing or in hot weather.
issues.why: Vans built through 2018 used Motorcraft Orange coolant, which can leave deposits that clog the radiator. Ford's bulletins (TSB 20-2150 and 21-2038) call for a flush, a new radiator if needed, and a change to Motorcraft Yellow coolant.
issues.next: Do not keep driving an overheating engine. Ask a dealer about the bulletin and do not mix coolant types.

issues.t: Weak heat or uneven heat side to side
issues.sym: The heater blows lukewarm, or one side of the van is warm and the other cold.
issues.why: Deposits from the coolant build up inside the heater core and block flow. Ford covers this in TSBs 19-2097 and 20-2053 for the gas engines.
issues.next: Have the heater core flushed or replaced, and switch to the newer coolant if the van still has the old orange type.

issues.t: Coolant leak at the thermostat housing or block heater
issues.sym: Coolant drips, a sweet smell, or the coolant level slowly dropping, often coming back after a repair.
issues.why: On 3.7L vans with an engine block heater, a worn O-ring or the intake-manifold thermostat housing can leak repeatedly (TSB 21-2408).
issues.next: Have the leak pinpointed with a pressure test and ask for the parts in the bulletin so it does not return.

issues.t: Six-speed automatic harsh shifts or bucking
issues.sym: Harsh or delayed shifts, slipping, bucking when accelerating, or a clunk when shifting from Park to Drive.
issues.why: Early vans had transmission and torque converter software that caused rough shifting. Software updates fixed many vans, but some needed internal repairs.
issues.next: Ask a Ford dealer for the latest transmission software. If shifting stays rough or it slips, get a transmission diagnosis before it gets worse.

issues.t: Driveshaft coupling can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Vibration, clunking, sudden loss of drive, or the van rolling in Park without the parking brake set.
issues.why: The flexible coupling that connects the driveshaft can crack and split. A loose driveshaft can also damage brake and fuel lines. NHTSA recalls 17V-408 and 19V-767.
issues.next: Use the parking brake every time you park until the recall is done. A Ford dealer replaces the coupling for free.

issues.t: Trailer tow module can take on water and short out (recall)
issues.sym: Turn signals, gauges or other electrical items acting up, or a burning smell near the module.
issues.why: Water can get into the trailer tow module and cause a short circuit and possibly a fire. NHTSA recalls 17V-668 and 18V-275.
issues.next: Have the free recall repair done, especially if you tow or the van has electrical glitches.

issues.t: Rear brake hose can leak fluid (recall)
issues.sym: A soft brake pedal, longer stopping distances, brake warning light, or fluid by a rear wheel.
issues.why: On early-built 2015 vans, the rear brake hose joints at the calipers could leak brake fluid. NHTSA recall 14V-482.
issues.next: Do not drive with a soft pedal. The dealer repairs it free.

issues.t: Sliding door missing reinforcement (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign; you may get a recall letter.
issues.why: Some sliding doors were built without epoxy reinforcement, so the door could unlatch in a side crash. NHTSA recall 14V-483.
issues.next: Check your VIN and get the free repair.

issues.t: Rear axle shaft can break (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the rear, sudden loss of drive, or the van rolling when parked.
issues.why: On a small number of 2015 vans, the rear axle shafts could fracture. NHTSA recall 15V-865.
issues.next: Use the parking brake and have the free recall repair done.

issues.t: A/C does not cool well
issues.sym: The air conditioning blows cool but not cold, often not getting the cabin below about 70 degrees on hot days.
issues.why: A/C performance was the top complaint for the 2015 Transit. Causes include leaking compressors, sticking air-door actuators and failed blower motors, plus the large cabin volume.
issues.next: Have the system checked for leaks and correct refrigerant charge. Ask a dealer about any A/C software or hardware updates for your build.

issues.t: Rear brakes wear out early
issues.sym: Grinding or squealing from the rear, a pulsing pedal, or rear pads worn to metal while the front brakes still look good.
issues.why: Heavy loads, stop-and-go delivery work and the way braking is balanced on the Transit cause owners to report fast rear brake wear, often in the 30,000-mile range.
issues.next: Have all four brakes checked at every oil change, not just the fronts. Replace rear pads before they reach metal to avoid buying rotors too.

issues.t: Power sliding door works only some of the time
issues.sym: The power sliding door will not open or close every time, stops partway, or a door warning comes on.
issues.why: Ford has bulletins for intermittent power sliding door operation (SSM 50699, TSB 22-2305). Manual sliding doors can also be hard to close and need adjustment.
issues.next: You can open and close the door by hand. Have a dealer run the bulletin checks for wiring, software and door adjustment.

issues.t: Boom or hum from the driveshaft
issues.sym: A booming, humming or moaning noise or vibration from the rear at certain speeds.
issues.why: On rear-wheel-drive, single-rear-wheel vans, the driveshaft U-joint at the transmission can cause noise and vibration. Ford updated the fix several times, most recently in TSB 24-2099.
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm the source and apply the latest bulletin repair, which may be covered under warranty.

issues.t: Misfires from poorly pressed valve seats
issues.sym: Rough idle, misfires, loss of power and a flashing check engine light.
issues.why: Some 2020 3.5L V6 engines were built with valve seats not pressed far enough into the cylinder head. Ford's program 20B21 replaces the cylinder head.
issues.next: Ask a Ford dealer to check your VIN for program 20B21. Do not drive far with a flashing check engine light.

issues.t: 10-speed automatic harsh or delayed shifts
issues.sym: A hard clunk when shifting into Drive or Reverse, harsh or late shifts, and sometimes a check engine light with codes P0772 or P2704.
issues.why: The 10-speed automatic used from 2020 has had many bulletins for harsh engagement and shifting, fixed with software updates, valve body or clutch parts, and a fluid cooler fix on early 2020 vans.
issues.next: Ask a Ford dealer to apply the latest transmission bulletin (such as TSB 23-2351 or 24-2100). Keep records if it keeps coming back.

issues.t: Rearview camera image distorted or missing (recall)
issues.sym: The backup camera shows a distorted, flickering or blank picture.
issues.why: A camera fault meant the image might not display properly. NHTSA recall 20V-575.
issues.next: Use the mirrors when reversing until the free repair is done.

issues.t: Driveshaft can separate (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking, vibration, sudden loss of drive, or rolling in Park.
issues.why: On some 2020 vans the driveshaft could separate. NHTSA recall 21V-978.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake, and get the free recall repair.

issues.t: Front passenger seat belt may not hold a child seat (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign.
issues.why: The front passenger seat belt retractor could switch out of its locking mode early, so a child seat might not stay tight. NHTSA recall 21V-592.
issues.next: Avoid putting a child seat in the front until the free repair is done.

issues.t: Defrost and climate controls can stop working (recall)
issues.sym: The climate controls go dead, including defrost and defog, so the windshield can fog up.
issues.why: A fault can make the HVAC controls stop responding. NHTSA recall 22V-791, with follow-up recalls 23V-122 and 25V-168.
issues.next: Pull over if you cannot clear the windshield. Get the free recall repair.

issues.t: Rearview camera image freezes or goes blank (recall)
issues.sym: The backup camera picture is delayed, frozen or black, or stays on after you shift out of reverse.
issues.why: Software errors in the camera system can stop the image from showing correctly. NHTSA recalls 23V-598, 25V-242 and 25V-315.
issues.next: Back up using the mirrors until the free software update is done. Some updates can be done over the air.

issues.t: Fuel tank vent valve may leak (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell or fuel leak near the tank.
issues.why: The fuel tank vent valve might not be properly welded, which can let fuel leak. NHTSA recall 23V-071.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, park outside and contact a dealer. The repair is free.

issues.t: Rear axle may run low on oil or use wrong bolts (recall)
issues.sym: Grinding or whining from the rear axle, the wheels locking up, or the van rolling in Park.
issues.why: Some rear axles were built with too little gear oil, which can wreck the bearings. A follow-up recall found incorrect axle shaft bolts on vans already repaired. NHTSA recalls 24V-102 and 24V-805.
issues.next: Use the parking brake every time and get both recall repairs done.

issues.t: Steering shaft bolt can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: Clunks or looseness in the steering, or loss of steering control.
issues.why: On some Transit Trail vans, an incorrect bolt on the steering column shaft could separate. A related recall covers a power steering ground that can corrode and cut assist. NHTSA recalls 24V-591 and 24V-542.
issues.next: Do not drive if the steering feels loose. Contact a dealer for the free repair.

issues.t: Engine crossmember may not be secured (recall)
issues.sym: Clunks under the hood, loss of drive, or a change in brake feel.
issues.why: On some vans the engine crossmember fasteners may not be tight, letting the engine shift. That can cause loss of drive power and possibly braking. NHTSA recall 26V-061 (Ford 26S04).
issues.next: Check your VIN and get the free fastener replacement.

issues.t: Brake pedal can disconnect (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal goes to the floor or does nothing.
issues.why: On about 16,000 2025 vans, the brake pedal could separate from the booster pushrod, causing loss of braking. Ford issued a 'do not drive' warning. NHTSA recall 26V-090.
issues.next: Do not drive an affected van until it is repaired. Have it towed to a dealer for the free repair.

issues.t: Body module freeze shuts off trailer and interior lights (recall)
issues.sym: Trailer lights or interior lights stop working.
issues.why: A software error can make the body control module freeze, switching off trailer and interior lighting. Ford recall 26C49 covers about 61,000 2026 vans.
issues.next: Check the trailer lights before towing. A dealer or over-the-air update fixes the software for free.

issues.t: Rear seat belt reminder may not work (recall)
issues.sym: The seat belt reminder does not show whether rear passengers are buckled.
issues.why: The wireless rear seat belt buckle sensor may fail to report buckle status. NHTSA recall 26V-579, covering 2026-2027 vans.
issues.next: Check that rear passengers are buckled yourself until the free repair is done.

issues.t: E-Transit rear halfshaft can pull out (recall)
issues.sym: Oil leaking from the left rear axle seal, loss of drive power, or the van rolling in Park.
issues.why: On about 32,000 E-Transits, the left rear halfshaft may not be fully seated in the drive unit, so its splines wear and it can come loose. NHTSA recall 25V-860.
issues.next: Set the electric parking brake every time you park and watch for leaks at the left rear wheel. Contact a dealer for the free repair.

issues.t: E-Transit battery tray rails can crack and let water in (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning before it is inspected.
issues.why: On some E-Transit chassis cabs, the side rails of the high-voltage battery tray can buckle and crack, letting water reach the battery and risking a short circuit and fire. NHTSA recall 25V-238.
issues.next: Park outside and away from buildings until the van is inspected. A dealer adds drainage holes or replaces the battery for free.

issues.t: E-Transit battery busbar washers may be missing (recall)
issues.sym: Possible warning lights or loss of power; often no early sign.
issues.why: Washers may be missing from bolts inside the high-voltage battery pack, which can cause high resistance and electrical arcing. Ford recall 26S05.
issues.next: Contact a Ford dealer to have the battery pack fasteners inspected for free.
